newsitem.title: FRANCE: Algeria smash rebel car smugglers network - radio.
newsitem.headline: Algeria smash rebel car smugglers network - radio.

text.p: Algerian security forces smashed a network of vehicle smugglers that supported Moslem guerrillas, Algerian state-run radio said on Monday.

Rachid Ben Abdelaziz, a security official, told Algerian radio the network of fundamentalist sympathisers had stolen trucks, cars and buses from some state-owned companies, such as Air Algerie, gas and electricity Sonelgas and vehicle maker Societe Nnationale des Vehicules Industriels.
The network's members then doctored official documents for the stolen vehicles and turned them over to Moslem militants for guerrilla activity, he said.

Security forces have so far seized more than 80 stolen cars, trucks and buses, worth 240 million dinars ($4.4 million), and arrested seven members of the guerrilla logistics support network, Ben Abdelaziz said.

He said the group was divided into "masterminds", cell members tasked to steal the vehicles, and a third category specialising in preparing documents and helping put the vehicles unnoticed back onto the streets.
"They were helped by people enjoying high places in society," the security official said without elaborating.
The Algerian authorities blame Moslem guerrillas for a series of car bombings in which thousands people have died in the past three years.

An estimated 50,000 people have been killed in Algeria's violence pitting Moslem guerrillas against government forces since early 1992 when the authorities cancelled a general election in which radical Islamists had taken a huge lead.
